title: Three FEROS spectra from 2020 show that the bright star of TYC 9179-1083-1 orbits the eclipsing pair; with the 2017 GALAH velocities, the pair-to-tertiary mass ratio is 1.18 +- 0.06
abstract: TYC 9179-1083-1 (TIC 300560295) is an eccentric 10.29-day eclipsing binary with a third star on a 5.9-year orbit found from TESS eclipse times. Campaign studies disagreed on the light of the third star, the inner geometry and the inner masses. We measured broadening functions of three public ESO FEROS spectra from 2020 (R = 48,000). Every spectrum shows a broad-lined star B (v sin i 12.4 km/s) at a constant 15.72 +- 0.23 km/s and a narrow-lined star A that follows the eclipse ephemeris with K1 = 54.70 +- 0.25 km/s. Star B gives 0.73-0.87 of the light at 4,450-6,860 Angstrom; this excludes the faint Gaia branch. The star-A velocities select the high-third-light inner geometry (w = 16.0 deg, 14.5-18.0; chi-square 0.2-0.8 for 1 dof) over the zero-light geometry (w = 0.5 deg; chi-square 42). The published inner masses 1.05 + 0.23 predict K1 = 22 km/s and fail; m2 is 0.51-0.70 solar masses for m1 = 0.6-1.1. With the GALAH 2017 velocities of a prior SCI study, star B slowed by 14.26 +- 0.51 km/s while the barycentre of the pair became 12.13 +- 0.39 km/s faster. These opposite changes show that star B is the tertiary and give M12/m3 = 1.18 +- 0.06 without a timing amplitude. The near-circular N-body outer orbit predicts the change (12.2-12.5 km/s); the Keplerian light-travel-time fits (14.1-14.4 km/s) do not, also after a refit with the high-light inner geometry. With the N-body mass function we get m1 = 0.63, m2 = 0.52 and m3 = 0.98 solar masses (about +-10 percent). Limitations: four spectroscopic epochs, chunk-scatter errors, assumed constant inner e and w from 2017 to 2020, and masses that depend on an N-body fit made with wrong inner masses. We give velocity forecasts for 2026-2031.

display.caption: Star B (circles) and the barycentre of the eclipsing pair (squares) move in opposite directions between GALAH 2017 and FEROS 2020; their ratio gives M12/m3 = 1.18. The N-body outer orbit predicts the 2017-2020 change of the pair velocity; the Keplerian LTTE fits predict too large a change.
Star A follows the 10.29-day eclipse orbit with K1 = 54.7 km/s; star B does not move. The three velocities select w = 16 deg, the high-third-light geometry, and reject the zero-light geometry.
FEROS broadening functions: a broad, constant star B and a narrow star A that moves by 65 km/s; BF differences remove star B.

citations.reason: Eclipse times, ephemeris, N-body and LTTE fits and code used; the assumed inner masses 1.05 + 0.23 fail the measured K1; the N-body outer orbit passes the two-epoch test, the LTTE fit does not.
Season e, w and inclination used; the velocities select its high-third-light geometry (w near 17.6 deg).
The measured light fraction of star B supports the bright astrometric branch and excludes the faint branch.
GALAH 2017 component velocities used as the second epoch; our K1 independently confirms its m2 range.
Spectroscopic light fraction and temperature order agree with its hot dominant tertiary.
Discovery of the deepening eclipses of TIC 300560295.
